species.name: Brammel

dex.text: A tangle of canes with two eyes in the dark middle. Nobody has ever been grabbed by it. A good many people have simply been caught.
dex.fact: Folklore says not to pick blackberries after Michaelmas, 29 September, because the Devil has been at them.

species.real: A bramble plant can root wherever the tip of an arching cane touches the ground, which is how one plant sprawls across a whole hedge.

species.name: Bramblemaw

dex.text: Has eaten the whole hedge and is now looking at the fence. Its mouth is a ring of thorns, and it is wearing its blackberries as eyes.
dex.fact: A blackberry is not a single berry but a cluster of tiny fruits, each with its own seed, called drupelets.

species.real: Blackberries are a hedgerow favourite for birds, mice and people alike, and the plant has been eaten in Britain since prehistoric times.
